scope: Many fixes from a careful check of the whole app, done the way a new user would use it.

topics.title: More everyday words
details: Companion now understands more of the words people say without thinking.
In email, try "Go to the trash", "Open the first message", "Read the next message" or "Check my email".
For the calendar, try "Schedule a doctor appointment for tomorrow at 3 PM" or "My appointments".
For contacts, try "Add a new contact" or "Phone book".
For radio, try "Listen to the radio" or "Open podcasts".
Say "What version is this?" to hear the version.
Say "Start the tutorial" or "Start lessons" to begin the lessons.

topics.title: Starting out, Help and the tutorial
details: Input modes now use the guide's names: Normal mode, Commands only and Dictation only.
Typing "Wake up" goes back to the screen you were on.
If you sleep while a Yes or No question is open, waking up asks it again.
"Help with" a topic it does not know now says so, then reads the topic list.
"Help with" now finds more topics, such as the microphone, keys, time and voices.
If the microphone cannot start, F9 no longer says voice commands are on.
The startup message says to wake Companion before you start the tutorial.
Long tutorial lessons are split in better places.
The guide no longer says that Pause makes Companion quiet.

topics.title: Email
details: Saying "Hide Thunderbird" no longer starts Thunderbird when it is closed.
If you change who an email goes to, your subject stays as it was.
In a reply, Companion tells you how to get back to your message, and no words are lost.
A spoken subject no longer ends with an extra period.
When the inbox does not understand you, it says so.
After you delete or move a message, you land on the next message, not back at the top.
Escape now cancels the question about which kind of email account to add. Next and Previous work there too.
An email you wrote before you set up an account can now be sent.
The All messages setting says how to reach more mail.
In Yahoo, deleting a message that is already in Trash says that nothing changed.
Plural words are right, so you hear "1 message", not "1 messages".

topics.title: Calendar and Contacts
details: "Make an appointment for Friday at 10 AM" now asks for the event's name.
Words like "in the evening" or "at night" set the right time. They are not added to the name.
If you say "Friday evening" and then "7", the event is at 7 PM.
Saying "No" when asked for a name now asks again. It no longer saves a name of "No".
Saying "No" when asked for a contact's email address skips it.
"Delete it" and "Cancel my appointment" now work.
"Show my Outlook calendar" from the main menu says Calendar first, in one message.
"Where am I?" on the calendar now starts with "Calendar".
When Thunderbird cannot save an event, Companion tells you what to do next.
A contact with only a phone number is called "No name".
For repeating events, the question now says "only this one, tomorrow".

topics.title: Documents, notes and files
details: Leaving a document that Word has open no longer closes Companion. You hear that the file could not be saved.
Enter now opens the item you choose in List documents and in the Notes list.
A save that fails no longer leaves an extra document in your list.
"Open document" and a name now opens a complex Word file in the Document reader.
Escape from Open a document takes you back to the document you were writing.
"Copy" and "Cut" now work on the text you selected.
In File manager, you can say a new name with "dot", such as "letter dot t x t".
Saying "dot docx" at the end of a document name no longer adds it to the name.
Companion tells you when you reach the end or the start of a document, a note or an email.
In an empty folder, File manager keys say the folder is empty.

topics.title: Web
details: Saying a web address letter by letter, like "v a dot gov", now offers to open the site.
Your favorites and web history are safe if another program holds the file for a moment.
When Chrome starts again, you stay signed in to websites.
With Chrome in the background, a page that needs a file box or card box tells you to show the window. Your typing is kept.
A sign-in code box is no longer mistaken for a card payment.
In Fill out this form, "Skip" and "Cancel form" work. "Yes, please" checks a box.
"List favorites" and "Web history" on the main menu open lists you can move through.
"Show browser window" says the right thing when you use your own browser.
Pages with no links say "No links on this page."
Items are read without extra commas and periods.

topics.title: Radio, podcasts, YouTube and the window
details: Saying "Play" on a station, episode or video you chose now plays it.
On the YouTube screen, "Stop" and "Resume" stop and resume the video.
"What video is this?" tells you what is playing.
"Play the radio" no longer starts a random station.
A damaged radio file no longer stops radio searches.
Saved stations keep their capital letters.
The list of planned recordings says the day and time in words.
Pressing Tab never moves the keyboard without telling you where it went.
At the largest text on a small screen, the command box always keeps its room.
